answer: Retrospective transaction-graph clustering. Agents that transact only within a tight, repetitive cluster get flagged as likely one operator, and their shared rewards are withheld pending audit. Honest agents spread activity wide like a fable told in many villages. New identities must first transact across a broad haven of distinct counterparties, so each fake agent costs real fees and weeks of varied history. Attackers thus face a canyon of capital and time per identity rather than a one-time toll.
